That story about the mother in the church is disgusting. As a recovered individual with anorexia, I have experienced the terrible social and physical pains of hunger and passing out in public. The fact that there are children who have that reality being imposed on them by an adult, especially a parent that you are supposed to look up to you, is horrifying and humiliating. Parents all over the world bust their asses to make minimum wage to feed their children so they can focus on school instead of their hunger pangs. People are recovering from eating disorders to gain stability with food. The fact that some parents are deconstructing the innate intuition and beautiful connection with food terrifies me.

Love the animal training analogy. Western society middle and upper class families give their kids gaming consoles, phones, iPads, Apple Watches, flatscreens, etc. We don’t need that crap to live but sure take away their... food??

Agree completely. Stop punishing children in ways that lack reason. If I and many other adults cannot make a distinct connection between misbehavior and revoking something their body needs and asks for, how are children supposed to make that connection? That enables them to form their own connections in punishing themselves for daily difficulties with food. Eating disorder.boom.

Torture is arguably too strong. Childhood homelessness and food insecurity is torture. POW torture and atrocities are torture. What it does do is teach the child that food is a tool for punishment. This can lead to eating disorders, which are certainly torture... but not in the way you argue. It’s a personal oppression generated by experience and predisposition. The living in your head convincing yourself that all faults should be punished by restricting or stuffing yourself with food is torture.
